transitions.historical_text: As long as this card remains on the field, negate the effects of Spell, Trap, and Monster Cards that affect a card(s) in the Graveyard, and neither player can remove cards in the Graveyards from play. transitions.modern_text: Negate the effects of Spells, Traps, and Effect Monsters that target a card(s) in either player's Graveyard. Cards in either player's Graveyard cannot be removed from play. All "Gravekeeper's" monsters gain 500 ATK and DEF.

(Lava Dragon's effect does not target), and outrank the UDE-era FAQ sentence and the retrospective EdisonFormat.com record. (Lava Dragon's effect does not target), so the modern card negates them at Edison as the period card did. What is left of a difference at Edison is effects that only affect a card in a Graveyard (Type, Attribute, Level), unresolved.

review.notes:
Escalation case. Upstream's pre-errata variant is a real historical implementation but of the wrong era for both formats this project covers, and its cdb text is a hybrid (text_matches_version index 6 at ratio 0.9543): it reads 'ATK/DEF' and 'Cards in the Graveyard' where the v6 printing reads 'ATK and DEF' and 'Cards in either player's Graveyard', while carrying the v6-only clause 'other than itself'. I record what I see rather than picking a lineage version for it. Chain starts at v2 because v2 is the newest text in force at the earliest snapshot the project covers; the older v0 (PGD-084, 2003-07-18) and v1 (DL3-001, 2004-02) 'all effects ... that involve Graveyards' are broader still and are noted here only. Trailing cosmetics after the last recorded change: v8 (MAMA-EN109, 2022-11-03) is the GY rewording and is what the pinned modern cards.cdb text matches; v9 (SBC2-ENF14, 2024-12-13) adds 'on the field', which both scripts already do via TargetRange LOCATION_MZONE. Note also that Necrovalley has no goat-entries.cdb variant at all, so upstream never modelled its 2005 behaviour either.

Round 037 (2026-09-29). Checked against period rulings: the differences the functional transition claims were searched for in the Konami-hosted UDE card FAQ (2008-12), the 2005 UDE card rulings page, Konami's errata lists, rulebooks and per-set ruling documents, and the archived UDE judge-list threads Yugipedia points to (the transition's rulings_check; docs/research/text-only-errata-audit.md, Necrovalley). No period ruling in the corpus settles a claimed difference, so the functional call stands unchanged (`unresolved` at both snapshots); the search is recorded in the check. The rulings read support d3 at both snapshots (the passages are in the check); nothing contradicts a claimed difference, so kind, summary and coverage are unchanged. The rulings read support d4 at both snapshots (the passages are in the check); nothing contradicts a claimed difference, so kind, summary and coverage are unchanged. [c3] d4 supported at Edison, supported at Tengu; d5 unresolved at Edison, unresolved at Tengu; d6 unresolved at Edison, unresolved at Tengu.
